ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is an inscribed triangle of circle $O$ with $OB$ and $OC$ connected. If the length of chord $BC$ is $2\sqrt{3}$, what is the measure of $\angle BAC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct OE $\perp$ BC at E. \\
Since OE $\perp$ BC, \\
then BE=EC= $\sqrt{3}$, and $\angle$BOE=$\angle$COE, \\
thus OE= $\sqrt{OB^{2}-BE^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}-(\sqrt{3})^{2}}=1$, \\
therefore OB=2OE, \\
hence $\angle$OBE=30$^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle$BOE=$\angle$COE=60$^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle$BOC=120$^\circ$, \\
which implies $\angle$BAC=\boxed{60^\circ}.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is an inscribed triangle of circle $O$ with $OB$ and $OC$ connected. If the length of chord $BC$ is $2\sqrt{3}$, what is the measure of $\angle BAC$ in degrees?
raw_record.answer: Construct OE $\perp$ BC at E. Since OE $\perp$ BC, then BE=EC=$\sqrt{3}$, and $\angle BOE=\angle COE$, thus $OE=\sqrt{OB^{2}-BE^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}-(\sqrt{3})^{2}}=1$, therefore $OB=2OE$, hence $\angle OBE=30^\circ$, thus $\angle BOE=\angle COE=60^\circ$, therefore $\angle BOC=120^\circ$, which implies $\angle BAC=\boxed{60^\circ}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a circle, points A, B, and C are on the circle, and triangle ABC is inscribed in the circle; point O is inside the circle, and two line segments OB and OC connected to chord endpoints B and C are drawn, so they represent radii. BC is a chord of the circle. In the currently visible image, there is no clearly distinguishable numerical marking of the radius length, and the text of the problem statement only explicitly gives BC=2√3.

Reasoning: According to the original figure intention required by the standard solution, the radius condition OB=OC=2 needs to be used; if this radius condition is completely not supplemented, ∠BAC cannot be uniquely determined only from the currently visible figure and BC=2√3. Under the condition of adopting OB=OC=2, draw OE⊥BC, with foot of perpendicular E. The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, so BE=EC=BC/2=√3. In right triangle OBE, OB=2 and BE=√3, therefore OE=√(OB²-BE²)=√(4-3)=1. Thus △OBE is a 30°-60°-90° triangle, and ∠BOE=60°. Similarly, ∠EOC=60°, so the central angle ∠BOC=120°. ∠BAC is an inscribed angle subtending the same arc BC, and is equal to half of the corresponding central angle, therefore ∠BAC=120°/2=60°.
